text_02: Evidence-based, relational, and grounded in your values.
text_03: My clinical work is rooted in Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), mindfulness, trauma-informed care, and compassion-focused approaches. I also integrate elements of non-violent communication (NVC) and motivational interviewing when we are working with behavior change or communication patterns.
text_04: In practical terms, this means we pay attention to your thoughts and feelings, but we don’t get stuck fighting with them. Instead, we practice noticing your inner experience with more spaciousness and compassion, and we explore what it would look like to move in the direction of your deeply held values—even when anxiety, self-doubt, or old patterns show up.
text_05: Sessions often include gentle exploration, guided awareness exercises, and concrete tools you can use between sessions. We might explore self-as-context (the part of you that can notice your thoughts and feelings without being overwhelmed by them), values clarification, boundary setting, or communication strategies that support more authentic, sustainable relationships.
text_06: Throughout our work, my intention is to offer a steady, attuned presence so that you have a consistent, grounded space to explore, experiment, and grow—at a pace that honors both your nervous system and your goals.
text_08: Learning to notice thoughts, emotions, and body sensations with curiosity rather than judgment or avoidance, so you have more choice in how you respond.
text_10: Clarifying what truly matters to you—connection, creativity, honesty, stability, growth—and taking small, doable steps in that direction, even in the presence of fear.
text_12: Moving away from harsh self-criticism and toward a kinder, more supportive inner stance that still allows for accountability, responsibility, and meaningful change.
